title: Favorite records and the one talk with Louis Armstrong
summary: Gil names Armstrong and Ellington records as his favorites and tells how his manager Joe Glazer kept them apart after one talk at the Astor Hotel.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But I would like to get back to ( ?) in music. And this doesn't restrict you to jazz or any particular type of music. But what are some of the things that you think if you had to be isolated, say in prison or a hospital or

anywhere. The desert island is just kind of a half joking thing of Sherman's. But in all seriousness, what are really some of your favorite things that you have never tired of? that really affect you emotionally?
I'm a sentimentalist and every time I hear 'Un Bel Di' (LAUGHTER). And I think that if I were ever isolated anywhere, I would want that with me.
Mine would be Louis Armstrong records. Duke Ellington, of certain periods.
Did you ever get to know him personally very well?
Never, no.
Never?
Never.
He never knew what an idol he was then?

We talked once. We had a serious talk one time, but that was the only time. At the Astor Hotel, if you remember they had given him those commercial awards they call it. Which was always for the one that sells
the most, but sometimes they coincided with the fact that they're good too. So that year he got it for 'Hello Dolly.' So we were waiting out Louis in the hall (
So we were there and I was telling him about all these old records and reminding him of this and that, you know. So he said, we should get together and possibly we can make an album.

So I went to see his manager. His manager was like a police dog, you know, wouldn't let you near him. He said, well one thing you have to remember is that Louis Armstrong is a very friendly man and he has a few drinks at night and he makes some promises and he was trying to make him out like a Chaplin millionaire, right? Kick you out of bed the next morning. So as a result that guy really kept us apart.
I thought, and then when I thought it over I realised what (
His name was Joe Glazer.
Oh yes. He was a villainous man. (LAUGHTER).
I saw him as a villain finally, in reference to Louis Armstrong I think he was a

villain because he caught him at a time when he was feeling very insecure. He had just seen King Oliver in his last days in destitution really when he shouldn't have been like that at all. And it shocked him terribly. And apparently he decided that this was never going to happen to him. So he signed with Joe Glazer and Joe Glazer paid him two thousand a week.
And collected all the rest for himself?

No, well he deposited and invested the rest for him. I don't know how much he stole. Naturally every, merchantry again right? You can't talk about that. But no, he saved it and gave Louis Armstrong two thousand a week salary out of it. But after a certain point he never did anything more. All he did was be a good entertainer and played. Up to a certain point he was creative on that trumpet (?).
I think he got pushed to do the things that made the money.
